# Source 103 — The Diplomat: With New AI Governance Organization, China Seeks to Formalize Its Global AI Influence

- **URL:** https://thediplomat.com/2026/07/with-new-ai-governance-organization-china-seeks-to-formalize-its-global-ai-influence/
- **Author:** Michael Caster
- **Published:** 2026-07-21
- **Type:** Analysis / opinion (The Diplomat, policy magazine)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- On **July 17, 2026**, Xi Jinping delivered the keynote at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai — the first in-person appearance by China's leader at the event since its 2018 launch.
- The **World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO)** was formally established a day before Xi's speech (July 16, 2026), to be **headquartered in Shanghai**.
- The idea of a China-led international AI organization was first proposed by Premier Li Qiang at the 2025 WAIC, building on China's 2023 Global AI Governance Initiative, and was reiterated in the Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) passed in March 2026.
- **29 countries signed** the WAICO establishment agreement on July 16, 2026. Founding members listed: Algeria, Cameroon, Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Lesotho, Mozambique, Oman, Senegal, South Africa (Africa/Middle East); Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan (Asia); Belarus, Russia, Serbia (Europe); Brazil, Cuba, Nicaragua, Venezuela (Latin America).
- In his keynote, Xi pledged over the next five years: **5,000 AI training opportunities** for developing countries; **AI cooperation centers** with ASEAN, the African Union, the League of Arab States, the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and BRICS; and inviting **30 countries to use China's AI-powered meteorological warning system, MAZU**.
- Xi framed WAICO as "a major move by China to answer the call of the Global South."
- Author's assessment: WAICO risks enshrining a state-centric ("digital authoritarian") model of AI governance; China's open-source push (e.g., Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 release timed with Xi's remarks) complements its diplomatic efforts.
